cameras.name: GoPro HERO11 Black
cameras.notes: All video H.265 (HEVC) in .MP4 (GoPro product page: max video bit rate 120Mbps; support article lists only H.265 bit rates). Per-mode nominal rates are published by GoPro (Standard/High/10-Bit columns) - not estimated. Frame rates as GoPro labels them (60/30/24 are NTSC-family 59.94/29.97/23.976 in practice; 50/25 PAL). 10-bit is offered only in 5.3K/4K 16:9 and 8:7 modes (N/A elsewhere); High for 4K 120 fps has no 10-bit. Extended Battery Video Mode uses lower caps (Standard 45-60 / High 60-120, e.g. 4K60 60/100) and Looping Video is 45 Mb/s - not listed as separate entries. No 9:16 recording mode in the HERO11 article. LRV proxy, audio and GPMF metadata add to card usage (GoPro capacity table shows ~2:01 per 128 GB at 120 Mb/s).

cameras.name: GoPro HERO12 Black
cameras.notes: H.265 (HEVC) only; gopro.com spec: 'Maximum Video Bit Rate 120Mbps', 10-bit (4K and higher). GoPro does NOT publish per-mode bit rates for HERO12 (variable bit rate, Standard/High setting); per-mode figures are derived from GoPro's 128 GB record-time table, scaled so 2:01 = 120 Mb/s (calibrated against HERO11's published table) - all estimated. 10-bit has no separate figure. 4:3 4K (4000x3000) exists only with Max Lens Mod 2.0 (60/50/30/25/24) - no rate data; 4:3 2.7K 60/50 listed in capacity table. Max Lens Mod modes not otherwise covered. Frame rates as GoPro labels them.

fixed.name: H.265 (HEVC) 5.3K (16:9) 60p High bit rate ~120 Mb/s
fixed.ref: Derived from GoPro support 'HERO12 Black: SD Card Capacity' table (128 GB card): 5.3K (16:9) 60 fps High bit rate = 2:01 (h:mm). Mbps = 120 x 121 min / 121 min = 120.0. Calibration: on GoPro's HERO11 Black capacity table (same 128 GB card) the published 120 Mb/s modes show 2:01, and this scaling reproduces several of HERO11's published per-mode rates (e.g. 5.3K60 Std 60 -> 62, 4K30 Std 45 -> 46, 1080p30 High 60 -> 61, 1080p240 High 78 -> 81), though that table is not consistent everywhere (4K30 High, published 100, shows 2:03), so treat as approximate. GoPro states HERO12/13 bit rate is variable with scene complexity; tables are static-scene estimates. 50 fps assumed same as 60 fps (PAL counterpart not in table).

Calibration: on GoPro's HERO11 Black capacity table (same 128 GB card) the published 120 Mb/s modes show 2:01, and this scaling reproduces several of HERO11's published per-mode rates (e.g. 5.3K60 Std 60 -> 62, 4K30 Std 45 -> 46, 1080p30 High 60 -> 61, 1080p240 High 78 -> 81), though that table is not consistent everywhere (4K30 High, published 100, shows 2:03), so treat as approximate. GoPro states HERO12/13 bit rate is variable with scene complexity; tables are static-scene estimates. 25 fps assumed same as 30 fps (PAL counterpart not in table).
